survey: A crystal ball on a gold stand, on a wooden shelf. The glass sphere is round and sits in a shallow gold cup. Its lower edge is hidden by the cup rim, which reads as the ball resting in the cup. The cup sits on a short gold neck and a wide, stepped round foot that sits flat on the shelf, with a contact shadow. Two curved gold prongs with ball tips rise from the cup rim to hold the sphere, one on the left and one on the right. The swirling mist and sparkle are inside the glass, which is the usual stylized look for a crystal ball and not an added part. The camera looks slightly down from the front.

errors.where: The two gold prongs holding the sphere
errors.what: The prongs should be mirror copies of each other, but they differ. The left prong leans outward and only grazes the outer edge of the sphere. The right prong is shorter, sits inward and crosses in front of the glass well inside its outline. So one prong barely holds the ball, and the pair does not grip it evenly.

fix: Make the stand's prongs a matching set placed evenly around the cup rim. Each prong should curve up the same way and press against the sphere's surface at the same height, so the stand clearly cradles the ball.
